idea: Harp puts Claude Code and Codex sessions in one sidebar and shows which one needs you.

claims.text: Harp runs many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one sidebar that shows which one needs you.
The README lists the sidebar states as needs you, background work, working, done and inactive.
Harp is an unofficial fork of the Warp terminal, licensed AGPL-3.0.
The README platform badge says macOS.

proof_plan.how_shown: sidebar scene with the needs-you row in view
sidebar scene, states named in narration

scenes.heading: WHICH AGENT NEEDS *YOU?*
scenes.say: You run several coding agents at once. One of them is waiting on you, and you only find out when you check the tab. This sidebar tells you which one.

scenes.heading: NEEDS YOU, WORKING, *DONE*
scenes.say: Harp groups your sessions by state. The README lists needs you, background work, working, done and inactive, so the blocked one is easy to spot.

scenes.heading: CLAUDE AND CODEX *LIMITS*
scenes.say: It also shows usage limit rings for Claude and Codex, so you can see how much room each one has left.

scenes.heading: THE *CATCH*
cons: Unofficial fork of Warp: read its terms first
pros: One sidebar for Claude Code and Codex
scenes.say: The catch: it runs on macOS only, and it is an unofficial fork of Warp, so read its terms before you ship.
Which tool do you run your agents in? Tell me in the comments.
